advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert `_SRC.is_dir()` and that the scanned file list is non-empty before asserting `not hits`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_no_old_model_defaults.py:47-48: `hits = [hit for path in sorted(_SRC.rglob("*.py")) for hit in _hits(path)]` / `assert not hits, ...`
Absence: nothing asserts that `_SRC` exists or that any files were scanned before `not hits` is treated as a pass.
advisory.finding: The guard test fails open. If `_SRC` resolves to a directory with no .py files (test moved, src layout changed, wrong `parents[...]` index), `rglob` returns nothing, `hits` is empty, and the test passes. A clean scan looks the same as a scan that never ran.
scenarios: The test file is moved to tests/unit/guards/, so parents[2] becomes tests/ and the path does not exist. rglob yields nothing and the guard passes forever.
advisory.suggested_fix: files = sorted(_SRC.rglob("*.py")); assert files, f"no sources found under {_SRC}"; hits = [hit for path in files for hit in _hits(path)]

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend `_old` to inspect string constants inside JoinedStr/BinOp values and keyword `default=` arguments, or narrow the module docstring to the exact shapes covered.
evidence: tests/unit/test_no_old_model_defaults.py:36: `candidates: list[ast.expr | None] = _assigned(tree.body)` — module scope only covers top-level statements
src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_emit.py:20: `_MODEL = f"anthropic:{VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL}"` — an f-string (ast.JoinedStr) holding an old id literal in this shape would not be flagged
advisory.finding: The scan only flags a value that is itself a plain `ast.Constant` str. It misses several common ways of hard-coding a default model: an f-string or concatenation (`f"anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"`, the same f-string pattern this change uses for _MODEL), dataclass `field(default="claude-...")`, env/getter fallbacks like `os.environ.get("X", "claude-...")`, and module-level assignments inside `if`/`try` blocks, because only `tree.body` is checked for module scope. This is narrower than the docstring's 'No default in src/rebar names a pre-5.5 Claude model'.
scenarios: Someone writes `_MODEL = f"anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"` or `model: str = field(default="claude-sonnet-4-6")` on a config dataclass, and the guard passes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the scan is live: collect the files scanned and check the list is non-empty and includes registry.py / fixture_emit.py before asserting `not hits`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_no_old_model_defaults.py:48: hits = [hit for path in sorted(_SRC.rglob("*.py")) for hit in _hits(path)]
tests/unit/test_no_old_model_defaults.py:49: assert not hits, "pre-5.5 Claude ids in defaults:\n" + "\n".join(hits)
Absence: nothing asserts that _SRC exists or that the rglob result is non-empty before trusting the empty `hits`.
advisory.finding: The repo-wide guard test only asserts that no hits were found, with no check that the scan read any files. If _SRC stops pointing at real source (layout move, wrong parents[] depth, package rename), rglob yields nothing, hits is empty, and the test passes without scanning anything.
scenarios: The src layout moves (e.g. to src/rebar_core), or the test file moves one directory deeper so parents[2] no longer reaches the repo root. Path.rglob on a missing directory yields nothing, so the guard keeps passing while a re-introduced "claude-sonnet-4-6" default goes undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: files = sorted(_SRC.rglob("*.py")); assert _SRC.is_dir() and any(p.name == "registry.py" for p in files), f"scan root {_SRC} found no sources"; hits = [hit for path in files for hit in _hits(path)]

The AST guard misses it too, because a dict-literal value is out of its scope.
